inputs.text: President John Mahama is declaring that our foundational policies must remain anchored in our established legal frameworks, longstanding cultural ethos, and the collective agreement of our society, rather than caving to outside influences. He's reaffirming his commitment to the rule of law amid these global human rights discussions. This kind of resistance to outside pressures is really about shielding entrenched power structures and historical inequalities from the reforms needed to end discrimination and protect vulnerable groups from ongoing exclusion and injustice.
